description.value: Malei Island Resort is a remote, off-grid, 45-acre wilderness lodge on Malei Island, reachable only by water taxi from Port Hardy. Guests experience old-growth rainforest hiking on a 2,800-foot boardwalk, whale watching, sea otter tours, and a salt-water wood-heated hot tub built into the rocks. The surrounding area was featured in the Netflix documentary 'Island of the Sea Wolves.'

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is live and describes a real, operating remote island resort accessible by water taxi north of Port Hardy, BC. The contact page confirms a phone number (1-778-347-3293) not present in OSM. The website has no mention of bicycle storage, bike procedures, laundry, Wi-Fi, or any cycling-specific amenities, so all those fields are null by absence-of-evidence. The resort is explicitly off-grid and island-based, meaning road-cycling access is impossible — a notable concern for a cycling directory.
concerns: Resort is on a remote island accessible ONLY by water taxi — not reachable by cycling; touring cyclists would need to transport bikes by boat.
OSM lat/lon places this in the ocean/island area near Port Hardy, consistent with the island location, but no civic address exists.
Terms of service lists company address as Mission, BC, which is the operator's office address, not the resort location.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating, publicly bookable business with an active website and phone contact. Accessible only by water taxi but may still be relevant to touring cyclists on multi-modal routes.

wow_evidence: featured in the Netflix documentary 'Island of the Sea Wolves'

price.label: Upscale
price.signal: off-grid private-island lodge with included wildlife tours, water-taxi access; package pricing above mid
